text:
incident-bot: PAGE @eng-oncall: Severity=P1 — Elevated latency and partial failures in eu-west-1 since 14:03 UTC after deploy r2026-03-17-3. Errors trending up, p95 up x3, some tail drops. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/latency-postdeploy. Please ack.

sasha: ack — oncall here. what's in that deploy?

dmitri: rolled runtime v2.8.1 to staged pool: kernel affinity tweak + new batching heuristics. Canary was green for 10m.

sasha: looking at metrics now — big p95 jump and throughput drop in pool infer-eu-2. Logs show kernel fallback -> generic kernels + batcher rejections.

sasha: snippet from worker log:
```
infer-runtime: kernel_fallback=true batch_reject_rate=1.3% mem_evictions=420
E 14:03:12 worker.go:214 batcher: reject due to mem_pressure
```

maya: KV cache eviction rate spiked at same time. evict/sec doubled. affinity tweak might be increasing working set per core.

eli: proposed live mitigations: 1) flip feature flag `batching-v2` off in eu-west-1, 2) revert traffic for rollout group -> stable variant, 3) enable rollout kill-switch to stop further waves. I can apply now.

ops-sre: executing revert and flag flip. Running: `redwood rollout revert --region eu-west-1 --to stable-2026-03-16 && redwood flags set batching-v2 false --scope region:eu-west-1`

incident-bot: ACTIONS TAKEN: rollout revert started, batching-v2=false applied. Estimated customer impact: degraded latency for ~8 orgs, ~4% of traffic.

sasha: confirmed kill-switch active and traffic shifting. p95 starting to trend down, throughput recovering. Will monitor for 2x stable windows. :white_check_mark:

dmitri: follow-up items: pin kernel affinity defaults, add mem-pressure preflight for batching heuristics, and add a canary ramp check for KV eviction. I'll open PRs and a postmortem.

maya: adding affected orgs to incident tracker and contacting CS for high-touch customers.

ops-sre: handoff: I'll keep monitoring until 15:30 UTC and coordinate customer comms. If p95 stays stable for 30m with no evictions, we close. Handoff ack.

sasha: thanks all — good mitigation. keep notes in the incident doc and assign postmortem owners.
